HERA RESEARCH · 6 NOVEMBER 2026

First exploratory models
on real logger recordings

Count-rate prediction using five independent flight recordings. The original screened tables remain marked unverified.

Scope: recorded cumulative-counter increments per elapsed second. These results do not establish calibrated physical flux, identical detector response, or a validated Pfotzer-peak altitude. Unknown flight-specific settings and clock assumptions remain part of the study.
918distinct 30-second intervals
5independent flights · 7.65 hours
2channels fitted separately

What was actually trained

For each channel, five XGBoost variants and a flight-balanced constant baseline were evaluated on each held-out flight. The run fitted 150 outer-fold XGBoost models and 2880 inner tuning models. Every interval received exactly one held-out prediction per variant and seed. Three random seeds repeat fits; they do not create additional independent flights.

Tuning used 24 candidates sampled with seed 2026, evaluated using four inner held-out flights and seeds 11, 42 and 73. The outer test flight was excluded from parameter selection. Training gave every flight equal total weight. Sensor derivatives were recomputed only inside contiguous retained intervals, without bridging excluded gaps. The analysis uses completed trajectories and is not a real-time forecast.

Primary scores average seed metrics within each flight, then average the five flights equally. MSE is in squared cps; RMSE and MAE are in cps. Averaging flight RMSE is different from taking the square root of average flight MSE. Negative R² means worse than that test flight’s own constant-mean reference. The CSVs also report between-flight spread, within-flight seed variation, ascent/descent scores and errors restricted to each phase’s training altitude min/max span. That span check does not prove dense training support throughout the range. Predictions below zero are clipped for scoring; SHAP explains the raw output.

The lowest descriptive XGBoost RMSE is Pressure only: 0.512 cps, 89.0% below the constant baseline. This comparison is descriptive; it is not a separately tested selection of a final winning model.

All 38 original package fingerprints matched before fitting. All 150 saved native models reproduced predictions after reload. The largest SHAP reconstruction discrepancy was 0.00001526 cps. All bundled input fingerprints still match. Seven preparation tests and six training tests passed.

Recovered project location and computer setup

The supplied preparation README records V:\Radiation_Profiles_Pfotzer_Peak_Estimation and .venv\Scripts\python.exe. Recovered base files are logger_preparation.py and prepare_logger_data.py, plus the frozen evaluation protocol. The original XGBoost notebook was not included. Older-chat retrieval was disabled, so the user’s exact CPU, RAM, GPU and Python version could not be confirmed. The execution environment recorded in run_summary.json belongs to this analysis environment, not the user’s computer. The supplied check_system.py reads local specifications and lists likely model notebooks without installing anything.

Remaining interpretation limits

  • per-flight hardware, thresholds, coincidence logic and orientation not fully documented
  • elapsed timer scale/wrap inferred; no independent UTC clock calibration
  • detector live time unavailable; targets are uncorrected recorded rates
  • same-row sensor snapshots need not be perfectly contemporaneous
  • no external tracking was supplied for August 21; top-board SD card damaged
  • The professor’s screenshot describes intended upward orientation, usual CosmicWatch use with occasional GMC counters, settings usually unchanged, and some coincidence operation. It does not supply exact settings or detector identities for every selected file. Counter labels are preserved without assuming inclusive channel populations.
  • No final production model was chosen from these test comparisons. No independent external validation or peak estimate is claimed.

Reproduce or inspect

Open README.md for Windows commands, dependency checks and fresh-output instructions. The results folder contains the metrics, held-out predictions, SHAP contributions, tuning evaluations, fitted models and their feature-order metadata. Figures for every XGBoost variant are included. No Google Drive writes were performed.

Methods: XGBoost prediction contributions; grouped cross-validation; nested parameter selection. Source screening and tuning plan: the unchanged HERA preparation package dated 23 October 2026.
